english.title: Prospective adopter fail to return child to adoption agency within 7 days of notice of section 35(2) notice
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the prospective adopter of **(..SPECIFY NAME OR IDENTITY OF CHILD..), a child who had been placed for adoption by **(..SPECIFY ADOPTION AGENCY..), an adoption agency which was of the opinion that the child should not remain with you and had given notice to you of its opinion, failed, not later than the end of the period of seven days beginning with the giving of the notice, to return the child to that agency
english.legislation: Contrary to section 35(2) and (4) of the Adoption and Children Act 2002.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: The local agency must act with procedural fairness (i.e problems should normally be raised and discussed). Where there is need for urgent return or return without notice, the correct course is for application to be made for Emergency Protection Order or Interim Care Order thereby involving Family Proceedings Court - see DL v Newham London Borough Council [2011] EWHC 1127

other.penalty:
Summary: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months and / or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions
6months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
